result.summary: Inlines and optimizes `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` and `arith_uint256` comparisons by defining them directly in headers using `std::tie`, `noexcept`, and C++20 `operator<=>`. Replaces the out-of-line `CompareTo` member function on `base_uint` with an inline per-word three-way comparison loop. Adds dedicated microbenchmarks across multiple work bit-widths, unit tests, and differential fuzz tests.
result.problem: Block index ordering in `setBlockIndexCandidates` and functions like `CheckBlockIndex` and `FindMostWorkChain` executes `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` heavily. The comparator and its underlying `arith_uint256` work comparisons were defined out-of-line with cascading conditionals, preventing compiler inlining and introducing unnecessary branch overhead.
evidence: Author's benchmarks show `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` throughput increases 6.5x–6.8x (from ~100M cmp/s to ~660-680M cmp/s across GCC and Clang) and `CheckBlockIndex` improves 1.4x–1.6x (from ~9-10k ops/s to ~14.4-14.8k ops/s).
result.scope_notes: Includes differential fuzz tests comparing the new comparator and arithmetic ordering implementations directly against pre-refactor snapshots.
result.changed_since_previous: Reorganized the commit stack to separate inlining from per-word `<=>` comparison changes, and extended the benchmark to test 12-bit and 96-bit chainwork cases alongside 256-bit cases.
result.card: This PR optimizes block index work comparisons by inlining `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` and `arith_uint256` three-way comparisons in headers using `std::tie` and `operator<=>`. It eliminates out-of-line function calls and branching cascades during candidate chain searches and validation checks. The author reports a 6.5x to 6.8x speedup in isolated work comparisons and a 1.4x to 1.6x speedup in `CheckBlockIndex`. Equivalence fuzz targets and deterministic sorting tests verify that work ordering and pointer tie-breaking behavior are unchanged. No dependencies are stated.

risk.why: A flaw in block index work comparison or tie-breaking could alter best-chain selection, potentially leading to chain forks or failure to activate the valid tip.
